stories.headline: Zelenskyy seeks EU funding as Starshield limits and US-Russia diesel deal strain ties
stories.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy asked European Union leaders in Brussels for nearly $80 billion in extra funding [c6]. He urged them to keep financing Ukraine's fight against Russia next year [c6]. Zelenskyy told the European Council that the war will cost €155 billion next year [c16]. He said that Ukraine needs at least €70 billion from the EU [c16]. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said a €70 billion funding gap must be covered for 2027 [c18]. Last year, the EU gave Ukraine a loan of about $100 billion, which equals €90 billion [c12]. To manage financial risks, Zelenskyy proposed an EU-controlled custodian for frozen Russian assets [c19]. European Council chief Antonio Costa said it is time to increase support for Ukraine [c9]. He also called for more pressure on Russia [c9].

At the same time, Ukraine faces major problems with its satellite communications network. Ukraine uses SpaceX's Starshield satellite system for battlefield communications [c3]. The army also uses it for mid-range strikes on Russian-occupied territory [c3]. It relies on the system for interceptor drones as well [c3]. On Tuesday night, Starlink restricted satellite internet speed limits to 100 mph, or 160 km/h [c13]. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Europe cannot replace Starlink's satellite internet capability in the short term [c11]. A bipartisan group of US senators signed a letter demanding an investigation into the network disruptions [c15].

There are conflicting reports about who ordered the limits on the system. Elon Musk said any limits on speed or usage were decided by the US military and the US president [c2]. But US President Donald Trump said on October 16 that he did not request a reduction in Starshield services [c1]. Zelenskyy said White House officials told his partners that they asked SpaceX to restore Starshield service [c4]. News agency Reuters reported comments from two US officials and a Western official [c17]. They said the order to slow down Starshield came from inside the White House [c17].

Tensions between Washington and Kyiv have grown over a trade deal. Trump struck a deal to buy Russian diesel on October 12 [c10]. The deal allows more Russian diesel into global markets [c5]. Zelenskyy criticized the move [c5]. Following this criticism, Trump called for Zelenskyy to be replaced [c5]. Trump also called renewed Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries a disgrace [c7]. Trump said he finds Zelenskyy more difficult to deal with than Russian President Vladimir Putin [c8].

Attacks on infrastructure continue to hurt civilians across Ukraine. Missile strikes hit energy and communications facilities, leaving around 600,000 people without power [c14].

stories.headline: Gunman kills four at Oregon school before armed bystander shoots him dead
stories.body:
A 16-year-old gunman killed four people at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon [c20]. Police identified the shooter as Griffin J. John II [c23]. He forced entry into the school by firing at locked doors [c30]. He used a Maverick 88 12-gauge pump-action shotgun [c24]. His mother had legally bought the weapon in August [c24].

The victims who died were five-year-old Rhoam Summer, an eight-year-old child, an 11-year-old child, and 25-year-old teacher Megan Lambert [c21]. Seven-year-old Saylor Graham and 54-year-old teacher Becky Drury went to the hospital with injuries [c22].

During the attack, a teacher confronted the gunman by throwing her phone and tackling him [c26]. An armed father driving past the school then pursued the gunman inside and shot him dead [c25]. US President Donald Trump called the armed bystander a great hero [c28]. The National Rifle Association said the incident showed the importance of armed citizens [c29]. Mourners later gathered at a memorial outside the school [c27].

deaths caused by violence or accidents

stories.headline: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia departs after five days in office
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump asked White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia to reconsider her job after five days [c32]. A White House official confirmed on October 16, 2026, that she was let go [c40]. Her five-day tenure was shorter than Anthony Scaramucci's 10-day stint as communications director [c37]. Zacharia had been appointed on October 9 to succeed Karoline Leavitt [c36]. At the time, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung called her uniquely qualified and whip smart [c39].

Zacharia graduated from Pepperdine University's law school in 2011 [c38]. But she later admitted she failed the bar exam and was not licensed to practise law, despite calling herself a lawyer [c33]. She also sparked anger during an interview by saying China does not even have proper toilets [c34]. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning advised Zacharia to visit China more often [c35].

vocab.meaning: the period of time that someone holds an official position
to take over a role or position after someone else

stories.headline: Fatal school roof collapse in Peshawar leaves dozens of children dead
stories.body:
A school roof collapsed in Peshawar, Pakistan, killing dozens of children and a teacher [c42]. Outlets reported different death tolls [c41] [c42]. A summary reported that 34 children were killed [c41], while the BBC reported that at least 33 pupils and one teacher died [c42]. The accident happened at the private Al-Khair school in Dir Colony [c42].

A total of 110 students were in three classrooms when the roof collapsed [c47]. At least 45 children were injured [c46]. Peshawar police chief Mian Saeed said the three-story building was overloaded [c44]. He said it was built with poor quality roof slabs [c44].

Police arrested the school owner after the collapse [c43]. Angry parents demanded accountability for the disaster [c41]. Faisal Karim Kundi, the governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, ordered a safety audit of all schools in the region [c45]. Pakistan spends less than 1% of its gross domestic product on education [c48].

vocab.meaning: below the required or acceptable quality level
responsibility for providing an explanation for actions or failures

stories.headline: Houthi missile strike on Aden presidential palace kills five people
stories.body:
Houthi rebels launched a missile attack against the al-Maashiq presidential palace in Aden [c54]. The strike killed five people and injured 16 others [c54]. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said their missiles hit the Saudi military operations headquarters in Aden [c55]. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said two Houthi missiles also landed near the runway at Aden International Airport [c49].

Fighting in Yemen has worsened recently. Yemen's health ministry reported that at least 1,282 people have died in fighting since August 6 [c56]. Military spokesman Majed al-Nazili said government forces killed over 430 Houthi fighters in Marib province in 24 hours [c50]. Saudi Arabia also intercepted a Houthi cruise missile over Medina province [c59]. Houthi strikes have targeted Riyadh's international airport 20 times this month [c58].

The UN Security Council condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and shipping [c57]. Iran denied involvement in Houthi operations and offered to mediate [c51]. Southern leader Aidarous al-Zubaidi called for troop mobilization and a secession vote in two years [c53]. Former Prime Minister Maeen Abdulmalik Saeed warned that losing Taiz would harm maritime security [c52].

vocab.meaning: killed or rendered unable to perform military actions
the act of formally withdrawing from a political state or union

stories.headline: Delhi Police detain 150 people during political protests over voter roll revisions
stories.body:
Delhi Police detained about 150 people in central Delhi during political protests [c65]. Opposition politicians and supporters from the INDIA bloc marched towards Jantar Mantar [c60]. They demanded the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar [c60]. Opposition parties accused Kumar of removing lakhs of voter names from electoral rolls [c62]. They said the deletions occurred through the Special Intensive Revision exercise [c62].

To maintain law and order, police enforced strict rules across central Delhi [c65]. Delhi Police imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita in Connaught Place [c66]. They also closed Central Park on October 16 and October 17 [c66]. Official guidelines specify that protests at Jantar Mantar cannot have more than 1,000 people [c61]. Organizers must also request permission 10 days before any rally [c61]. Cockroach Janta Party co-convenor Saurav Das had submitted an intimation letter at Parliament Street police station for an October 10 protest [c63].

Police stopped key political figures before the planned Lehra Do Tiranga protest [c64]. Officers detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke [c64]. Police sources said officers caught Dipke at Jhandewalan as he travelled towards Connaught Place [c68]. Party leader Rohan Deshpande wrote to the station house officer at Mandir Marg police station [c69]. He asked for details about Dipke's location and the legal reasons for his detention [c69].

Police also detained All India Students' Association president Neha Bora [c64]. Communist Party of India (Marxist) lawmaker John Brittas said police took Bora at Mandi House [c70]. He said she was on her way to join the protest [c70]. Lawyer Supantha Sinha said police took Bora into custody around 5:00 pm [c67]. Sinha added that police only revealed Bora's location at RK Puram police station around 10:30 pm [c67].

vocab.meaning: serving to forbid or restrict specific actions by law
an official notification or formal announcement

stories.headline: US police arrest teenager planning attack on Illinois Hindu temple
stories.body:
US police arrested a 19-year-old man for planning a shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois [c71]. Alexandros Paporakis was arrested on October 11, 2026, in Palatine near Chicago [c71] [c76]. Palatine Police Chief William Nord said a colleague alerted police after getting troubling messages from Paporakis [c78]. Authorities said Paporakis drove to the Sri Venkateswara Temple in Aurora on Sunday [c79]. His rifle jammed when he tried to shoot [c79].

US Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi said he and his family were at the temple during the attempted attack [c73]. At Paporakis' home, police found a rifle, ammunition, loaded magazines, and body armour [c77]. Investigators found a manifesto expressing white-supremacist hatred toward Indian, Jewish, and Black people [c74]. Paporakis was charged with illegal weapons possession and making a terrorist threat [c76]. Over 50 US officials condemned the attack [c75].

India's Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal urged US authorities to protect Indian nationals [c72]. A study found online hate against South Asians in the US grew 240% from 2024 to 2026 [c80].

vocab.meaning: a public written declaration of beliefs or intentions
designed or suitable for military or emergency actions

stories.headline: Indian opposition criticizes government over upcoming Marco Rubio meeting in Mumbai
stories.body:
Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar will host US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Mumbai on October 20 [c81]. Rubio will arrive on October 18 for his second India visit of 2026 [c91]. He aims to strengthen energy cooperation [c84]. Rubio will visit Mumbai and Jamnagar [c86]. In Jamnagar, he will tour Reliance facilities linked to a Texas refining project [c87]. Jaishankar will also attend US independence anniversary celebrations in Mumbai as guest of honour [c83].

Before meeting Rubio, Jaishankar will host UAE Deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Mumbai on October 19 [c82].

The visit sparked domestic criticism. US Ambassador Sergio Gor first announced the meeting at a forum [c88]. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh asked why the US ambassador announced Jaishankar's schedule instead of Indian officials [c89]. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi claimed on social media that Rubio summoned Jaishankar [c85]. Trade relations have been sensitive after the US put a 25% tariff on Indian goods in 2025 over Russian oil buys, which was removed in February 2026 [c90].

vocab.meaning: relating to internal affairs within a country
involving or agreed upon by two official parties or countries
